learningObjective: Given a GEMM followed by a pointwise chain, decide which fusion form (epilogue vs. separate kernel) is expressible and legal.
stem: The IR above shows a GEMM followed by a bias-add and GELU, and a proposed rewrite that folds them into a matmul epilogue. Which condition is required for the rewrite to be legal AND to deliver the intended memory-traffic benefit?

options.text: The rewrite is always legal because bias-add and GELU are pointwise; the memory benefit is automatic and independent of how the compute op streams its output.

The GEMM implementation must expose an epilogue slot that writes each output tile only after applying the pointwise chain in registers; without this, the pointwise ops still read/write the full M×N output via DRAM and no traffic is saved.
The rewrite is legal only if `bias` has shape `[M, N]` (same as the GEMM output); a broadcast `[N]` bias cannot be fused into an epilogue.
The rewrite is legal only when M×N is a multiple of the warp size, otherwise the epilogue introduces a tail block that violates SSA form.

explanation: Legality of the rewrite is a pattern match on pointwise-after-GEMM; the intended traffic benefit only materializes when the GEMM kernel actually applies the epilogue to each output tile in registers before writing back to DRAM (as in cuBLAS Lt / CUTLASS epilogues). If the compiler emits a standalone GEMM plus separate pointwise kernels, the pointwise ops re-read the M×N tensor from DRAM and the fusion is 'logical' but has no memory-traffic benefit. Broadcast bias `[N]` is a supported epilogue pattern in cuBLAS Lt and CUTLASS. Warp-size divisibility affects tile boundaries but not SSA legality.

optionExplanations.A: Wrong: legality alone does not deliver the traffic saving; the compute op must expose an epilogue path.
optionExplanations.B: Correct: this is the essential precondition — the GEMM kernel must fuse the epilogue in-register at tile granularity.
optionExplanations.C: Wrong: broadcast biases are a standard epilogue pattern in cuBLAS Lt / CUTLASS.
optionExplanations.D: Wrong: tail-block handling is a scheduling concern, not an SSA violation.

assumptions: The GEMM is implemented by a library or generated kernel that supports epilogue fusion.
Bias and GELU are pure and side-effect free.
nonImplications: Does not imply epilogue fusion is always faster in wall-clock; small M×N or memory-bound follow-ups can flip the trade-off.
Does not imply cuBLAS Lt supports every arbitrary pointwise chain; supported epilogues are a fixed catalog.

distractorRationales.A: Ignores the difference between logical fusion at IR level and physical fusion at kernel level.
distractorRationales.D: Introduces a spurious SSA claim about tail blocks.

performanceClaim.scope: GEMM + bias + activation epilogue on Tensor-Core capable GPUs
